text:
elaine: Heads-up — saw a regression on canary GPUs this morning. Continuous-batcher assembled an 18-slot batch and the KV cache on g3-021 spiked, followed by OOMs and kernel fallbacks. Posting quick profile link: https://internal.redwood/p/5332/profile
rohit: Can you paste the tail of the allocator logs and the batch composition? My suspicion is admission isn't accounting for per-token KV footprint when many long requests align.
maria: Log snippet from g3-021 (trimmed):
```
[allocator] kv_capacity_bytes=25769803776
[allocator] kv_used_bytes=23192823360
[batcher] assembled_slots=18
[batcher] slot_tokens=[120,240,90,180,200,160,150,130,110,95,85,300,210,140,100,75,60,50]
[error] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[recovery] kernel_fallback=cpu
```
elaine: Also attached the microprofile peaks — KV cache grows ~3.2GB during peak assemble window. Worth noting kernel selection bumped to slower kernels after fallback which spiked tail latency.
rohit: Thanks. Proposed short-term mitigation: admission that computes a remaining token budget from KV bytes instead of a static token count. Rough sketch: available_kv = kv_capacity - kv_used - safety_margin; per_token_kv = model_kv_bytes_per_token; max_tokens_batch = floor(available_kv / per_token_kv). Then admit slots until sum(tokens) <= max_tokens_batch. That prevents oversubscription even when many big requests align.
maria: That makes sense. We should also add a soft slot cap (slot_soft_limit) to avoid crazy slot counts with many tiny requests that still hit kv bookkeeping.
rohit: Agreed. Example pseudo-config to try on canary:
```yaml
batcher:
  token_budget_mode: dynamic_by_kv
  kv_safety_margin_bytes: 2147483648  # 2GB
  slot_soft_limit: 12
  per_token_kv_bytes_by_model:
    llama-70b: 64
    redwood-13b: 48
  canary_fraction: 0.10
```
rohit: And simple admission algorithm:
```
available = kv_capacity - kv_used - kv_safety_margin
per_token = lookup_per_token_kv(model)
max_tokens = floor(available / per_token)
batch_tokens = 0
for req in queue_order:
  t = min(req.requested_tokens, max_tokens - batch_tokens)
  if t <= 0: hold(req) else admit(req, tokens=t); batch_tokens += t
```
tony: Two things to call out: 1) kernel selection depends on sequence length distribution — if we trim tokens per-slot we may push more flows to shorter-kernel paths (good) but also increase context-switching and reduce kernel occupancy. 2) fallback kernels buy memory but cost 2-6x latency; add a fast metric to detect when we trade cost for huge latency regressions.
maria: Ops checklist for the canary: emit these metrics for the next 6h: batcher.admit_rate, batcher.hold_rate, kv.eviction_count, kv.oom_count, kernel.fallback_count, tail_p99_latency. If p99 rises >20% revert.
elaine: I'll flip the canary token_budget_mode and kv_safety_margin on 10% canary nodes now. Will stream logs to #eng-runtime and drop a short repro if it reproduces locally.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout of config "batcher.dynamic_kv_budget.v1" -> canary fraction 10% (nodes: g3-020,g3-021,g3-022). Monitoring hooks enabled.
maria: Make sure to tag the canary with a unique trace id so we can filter metrics easily (tag=cache-cushion-canary-554321). Also capture one sample of full batch composition every 30s.
elaine: ack. will report back by EOD with metrics and any regressions. If anyone has objections to the 2GB safety margin, speak up now — otherwise we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
